scope.description: Selected Guerber Pandora passages cover Mercury's arrival, Pandora's opening of the box, the release of evils, Hope remaining, and Hope's later release.
scope.boundaryRationale: The record follows the core event sequence and explicitly lists omitted adjacent passages, including poetry and additional dialogue.

evidence.sourceText: Pandora immediately ceased dancing, to speculate with feminine curiosity upon the contents of the chest.
She nudged Epimetheus, and in a whisper begged him to ask Mercury what brought him thither.
One lovely evening, while dancing on the green, they saw Mercury, Jupiter's messenger, coming towards them.

Now, Jupiter had malignantly crammed into this box all the diseases, sorrows, vices, and crimes that afflict poor humanity; and the box was no sooner opened, than all these ills flew out, in the guise of horrid little brown-winged creatures, closely resembling moths.

It was well for Pandora that she opened the box a second time, for the gods, with a sudden impulse of compassion, had concealed among the evil spirits one kindly creature, Hope, whose mission was to heal the wounds inflicted by her fellow-prisoners.

events.sourceText: Lightly fluttering hither and thither on her snowy pinions, Hope touched the punctured places on Pandora's and Epimetheus' creamy skin, and relieved their suffering, then quickly flew out of the open window, to perform the same gentle office for the other victims, and cheer their downcast spirits.
